source_note: PRS Legislative Research, Union Budget 2024-25 Analysis (Expenditure Budget, Union Budget 2024-25)

sectors.name: Defence
ground_reality: Capital outlay: ₹1,72,000 crore (27.7% of total defence allocation), up 20.3% from 2023-24 actual expenditure.
75% of the modernisation budget (₹1,05,518 crore) is earmarked for procurement through domestic industries under 'Aatmanirbharta' in defence.
₹92,088 crore allocated for sustenance and operational readiness — maintenance facilities, ammunition procurement, resource mobility — a 48% increase over FY 2022-23.

Revenue vs capital split and multi-year procurement timelines for specific platforms are not itemised in the public budget document at this level of detail — verify against CAG defence audit reports for project-level figures.

sectors.name: Road Transport & Highways
ground_reality: This ministry's allocation grew 25% in 2023-24 alone, driven largely by increased investment in NHAI (National Highways Authority of India).

Project-level rework/maintenance-vs-construction-cost data is NOT available from the budget documents alone — this requires NHAI's own project completion reports and CAG performance audits of specific highway stretches, which have not yet been ingested into this dashboard.
See this dashboard's 'Land Allocation' topic for CAG findings on specific road-linked land and contract irregularities already sourced (e.g. Karnataka KIADB, Noida Authority cases).

sectors.name: Railways
ground_reality: Railways allocation grew 48.6% in 2023-24, the single largest percentage increase among the top 13 ministries that year.
Freight revenue reporting and station/track modernisation project-level data would need direct ingestion from Ministry of Railways annual reports — not yet connected here.

sectors.name: Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
ground_reality: Food subsidy alone is estimated at ₹2,05,250 crore in 2024-25, a 3.1% decrease from actual 2023-24 expenditure — the large majority of this ministry's total allocation.
Distribution-level data (ration shops, leakage estimates, Public Distribution System audits) would need ingestion from state-level PDS audit reports, not yet connected.

sectors.name: Home Affairs
ground_reality: Covers central police forces, internal security, and Union Territory administration.
Granular breakdown (force-wise deployment costs, infrastructure spend) not available at budget-document level — would need Ministry of Home Affairs annual report ingestion.

sectors.name: Rural Development
ground_reality: MGNREGS (rural employment guarantee) has the highest single scheme allocation in this ministry at ₹86,000 crore — unchanged from the 2023-24 revised estimate.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (rural housing) allocation: ₹80,671 crore, up 49.1% over the 2023-24 revised estimate — though actual 2023-24 expenditure fell 32% short of its own budget estimate, mainly due to the rural component underperforming.
This underspend-vs-allocation gap is exactly the kind of 'ground reality vs promise' figure worth tracking further at the state level — not yet broken down by state in this dashboard.

sectors.name: Chemicals & Fertilisers
ground_reality: Predominantly fertiliser subsidy (urea and nutrient-based subsidy schemes).
State-wise or crop-wise subsidy distribution data not available from the top-level budget document — would need Department of Fertilizers scheme-level data.

sectors.name: Others
ground_reality: Consolidates every remaining ministry and expenditure head — including Education, Health, Agriculture, Environment/Forest & Climate Change, Communications, and interest payments (which alone are 24% of total central government expenditure).

Health: the Interim Budget 2024-25 allocated ₹98,761 crore to the health sector (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare receiving 92.1% of that), a 2.6% increase from the previous budget estimate — but health expenditure as a share of GDP continues to fall short of the National Health Policy's 2025 target, per independent budget analysis (CBGA India).
Education-specific allocation figures were not confirmed in the sources checked for this update — flagged for a follow-up search rather than estimated here.

This 'Others' category is intentionally broad per the brief's own 8-tile structure — each of these sub-sectors deserves its own dedicated breakdown, which is what this dashboard's individual topic pages (Deforestation, Land Allocation, etc.) are for.
